Subject: Sizing & term tradeoffs for reserved capacity - Acme AI (ACME-129)

Team —

Quick ask ahead of today's call with Acme: they want a committed fleet proposal tied to expected Q4 latency SLAs. Acme is evaluating both a 12-month and a 24-month reserved capacity term; procurement prefers 12m but they only have budget for ~60% of the baseline GPU hours we estimated.

Top questions for the call:
- If Acme commits to 12m vs 24m, what incremental per-token/unit discount bands do we need to hit to make the math work for them?
- At what % of baseline committed utilization do we have to carve out burst/pool capacity to protect other customers?
- What approvals are required internally for discounts beyond standard tiers? (need that answer live)

I've attached the capacity workbook with our baseline run rates and a compact sensitivity table (acme_capacity_estimates.xlsx).

Can Marcus and Karthik bring a quick sensitivity breakdown and recommended approval thresholds?

Thanks,
Vanessa

Vanessa —

Quick sensitivity summary below (pulled from the workbook):

Baseline: 400 GPU-hours/day equivalent (mixed A100/RTX mix)
Assumptions: 70% average utilization on committed pool; 30% burst capacity requested for peak Q4 windows

Scenario A - 12m commit (60% of baseline):
- Committed pool: 240 GPU-hrs/day
- Expected utilization of committed pool: 85% (they will drive steady traffic)
- Cup & burst: we recommend reserving 120 GPU-hrs/day as burst on shared pooled capacity (auto-burst)
- Sensitivity: if effective GPU cost rises 15%, unit cost increases ~9% on their committed usage unless we increase discount by ~8-10%

Scenario B - 24m commit (100% of baseline):
- Committed pool: 400 GPU-hrs/day
- Expected utilization: 80%
- Burst: 0-40 GPU-hrs/day as planned overtime buffer
- Sensitivity: 15% GPU cost spike -> unit cost increases ~5% given longer-term hedging; discount bands can be ~12-18% and still meet our margin floor

Recommendation: Offer a deeper discount for 24m to reflect hardware cost hedging (14% target). For 12m, offer a smaller concession (8-10%) but include priority burst credits and a volume-based true-up at quarter boundaries.

I'll be on the call and can walk through the numbers.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Adding pricing perspective: standard discount tiers are:
- 10-14%: field-level approval (AM + Revenue ops)
- 15-24%: CRO approval required
- 25%+: Executive approval (CFO/CRO) and finance signoff

Given Marcus' recommendation, the 14% for 24m is borderline CRO territory, and 8-10% for 12m is fully within field authority.

Proposed commercial structure for negotiation:
1) 12m option: 10% off list on committed usage; 2 quarters of burst credits (pre-bought) included; quarterly utilization true-up with credits applied.
2) 24m option: 14% off list on committed usage; 6 months of burst credits; price reset clause tied to GPU cost index if spot GPU cost moves >20% for more than 2 consecutive quarters.

If Acme pushes for deeper discount (>=25%), we need to loop in Evelyn and prepare a short margin impact memo for finance.

Karthik
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clarity, Vanessa/Marcus/Karthik. A few clarifications from our side before the exec review: 

1) Budget: Finance will likely sign off on up to 65% of your baseline for a 12m term if the effective unit price is within 12% of our current cloud spend. 24m is preferred by our CTO but only if we can lock a price cap mechanism.
2) Bursting: we need at least 20% guaranteed burst in all quarters — anything less will break our SLAs with end customers.
3) Contract: procurement prefers a 12m starter with an option to extend at pre-agreed pricing tiers (we don't want to be re-priced mid-stream).

We can take the 12m with the 10% concession if you include the quarterly true-up and the burst credits. If there's a documented price cap tied to GPU-cost index for longer terms, that would make 24m attractive.

Will schedule our internal exec review tomorrow and loop back.
